fold: You come into <N> by a gate, and someone at the gate sees you come.
text: You come into Grímthorpe by a gate, and someone at the gate sees you come.
why: Says everyone enters by a gate and is seen; smugglers have ways in beneath the walls, a share of arrivals never reaches the gate, and the port brings ships

fold: The supply book for <N>'s defenders runs short: the trades that should feed and equip them are failing, so the defence is weaker than its numbers suggest.
text: The supply book for Grímthorpe's defenders runs short: the trades that should feed and equip them are failing, so the defence is weaker than its numbers suggest.
why: Says trades feeding and equipping defenders are failing; LAND gives Standing Garrison and Mercenary chains only vulnerable, defence Fortress, and C20189 says defenders properly equipped

fold: Whatever reaches <N> by road reaches it at a gate, and the town can close them against it.
text: Whatever reaches Megalchorion by road reaches it at a gate, and the town can close them against it.
why: says the town can close the gates; under occupation the garrison is under occupier command and officers do not rule freely

text: Reiko Ryu has food, enough to matter.
why: Fish-market master 'has food, enough to matter' under famine whose failed source is fish; LAND has River Fisheries depleted, fish imported salted

fold: The church and the garrison in <N> act as #: soldiers keep the feast days, priests stand at the musters, and an offence against the faith is answered by armed men who call themselves crusaders.

why: Church and garrison 'act as one'; C7776 says each wishes the other would keep quieter; QUARRELS/relations list no tie between Religious Authorities and The Garrison Bloc

why: 'Organized criminals now outweigh the law' but the page says crime is unorganized, diffuse, each working alone, no boss
